name: Aero L-39 Albatros
summary: Czechoslovak jet trainer used by Warsaw Pact air forces; the most common privately owned jet warbird in the US.

wings: Permanent fuel tanks on the wingtips
engines: Single turbofan with small intakes on both sides of the fuselage behind the cockpit
fuselage: Tandem two-seat cockpit with a stepped canopy (rear seat raised)
tail: Horizontal tail mounted on the fuselage below the fin

tellTales: Straight wing with permanent tip tanks on a small jet trainer
Side intakes behind a stepped tandem canopy
Short, stubby fuselage with a pointed nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The T-38 is a slim twin-engine jet with thin swept wings and no tip tanks; the L-39 has a straight wing with tip tanks.
The Goshawk has a swept wing with no tip tanks; the L-39 has a straight wing with tip tanks.
The L-29 has a rounder pot-bellied fuselage, straight wing with no tip tanks and a more bulbous nose; the L-39 is slimmer with a tapered wing and tip tanks.
The Iskra is a slimmer jet with a straight wing and wing-root intakes under a long single canopy; the L-39 has larger fuselage-side intakes and wingtip tanks.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
